headline: Researchers at Google and MIT propose linking many small flat quantum chips in a hyperbolic pattern so that error correction needs more than 30 times fewer physical qubits.
score_reason: Large claimed saving, but a preprint on arXiv with circuit simulations only, no hardware and no peer review reported.
importance_line: If it holds up on real devices it could make large error-corrected quantum computers more buildable from modest chips, which matters to hardware makers; the figures come from simulation in a preprint and have not been shown on hardware.
summary: Quantum Computing Report reports that researchers at Google Quantum AI, Google DeepMind and MIT propose, in a preprint on arXiv, linking small flat chips of about 100 qubits along their edges to run a more efficient type of error-correcting code, needing over 30 times fewer qubits than the standard surface-code approach. The result comes only from computer simulations, which held up even when links between chips were 10 times noisier than operations on a chip.
notes: Read Quantum Computing Report article (ext fetch via curl; fulltext file was empty). arXiv paper not read directly. Simulation only.
